title: Floors
description: New floors from the tower, and a floor's repos: a floor for a folder that already holds a project, a git repository cloned from its URL as a job, or a new project started from scratch, added to the config through config/add; a floor's repos changed through config/append and config/remove.

add.description: Add a floor whose hub is a folder that already exists, such as a project already on the machine, with the other folders its sessions also work in as its repos. Refused when a folder doesn't exist, a repo is the hub or is named twice, or the config already has a floor of that id.

name.description: The name the floor is shown by.

hub.description: The absolute folder its sessions start in by default; the new-worker form can start one elsewhere.

repos.description: Other absolute folders its sessions also work in, none when left out: each must exist and not be the hub.

words.hint: a floor for a folder already on the machine

clone.description: Clone a git repository from its URL into a new folder as a job of the jobs daemon, so a restart of the tower doesn't stop it, then add a floor whose hub is that folder once it ends with exit 0. Nothing types into a job: a repository that asks for a password or a host key fails, saying so (set up an SSH key or a credential helper). The job's argv, with the URL, is kept in the jobs log for as long as the log is kept, and its env never: a URL carrying credentials is refused. Refused when the floor's id or the folder is taken, or held by a clone in flight, or the folder exists and isn't empty.

guidance.brief: New floors: `tower x floors add|clone|start` adds a floor for a folder, a cloned repository or a new project; `add-repo` and `remove-repo` change its repos.
guidance.full: When the user asks for a new floor or to change a floor's repos, use this extension's verbs rather than editing config.json by hand: `add` for a folder already on the machine (`{"id", "name", "hub", "repos"?}`), `clone` for a git repository by URL (`{"id", "name", "url", "into"}`: a job that outlives the tower; the floor is added when it ends with exit 0, and `board.x.floors.clones` says where each stands), `start` for a project from scratch (`{"id", "name", "into"}`, a git repository with a first commit), `add-repo` and `remove-repo` (`{"project", "path"}`) for the other folders a floor's sessions work in. A failed clone: `remove` deletes what it left, `retry` clones again, `dismiss` forgets it (each `{"job"}`). The hub is where its sessions start by default; repos are other folders they also work in. `tower x floors dirs '{"path": "/abs"}'` lists a folder's folders.

clones.description: What floors did about each clone it ran as a job, by job: the clone it started and the floor it is for, the floor it added from it, why adding it was refused, and a clone the user dismissed. What a clone came to is the job's, read from board.jobs.

s.description: A clone started as a job: the floor it is for and where it goes.

a.description: The floor added from a clone that ended with exit 0.

r.description: Adding a clone's floor was refused, and why: the trigger leaves it to the user.

d.description: A clone the user dismissed, or retried as another job.

clones.description: Floors' clones whose job the board holds, newest first: each the floor it is for, what its job came to (running, cloned, failed, cancelled, lost) and what floors did about it.
